clue.text: Theologian has a hard conclusion to ponder

indicators.note: a conclusion comes at the end, so these letters are tacked on after the verb for pondering

blocks.note: to mull something over is to ponder it
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A religious scholar faces a tough ending to some question he must think over.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullah is a Muslim scholar trained in Islamic law and doctrine, a religious teacher.

clue.text: One that's near getting fit for blue

blocks.note: near is an old word for stingy, and a miser is stingy
fit and able both mean capable

explanation.surface: Someone close by is getting kitted out in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' means close at hand on the surface, but in older British usage it means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is an idiom for being sad or downcast, which is to be unhappy and low.

clue.text: Skin spots fast disappear when iodine's absorbed

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so the chemical symbol goes within the other letters

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
to go is to vanish
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Iodine applied to blemishes makes them vanish quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quickly, but it is the noun for abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is the medical term for small brown pigmented patches on the skin, such as freckles.

clue.text: Leaves producer in American ski resort

blocks.note: first meaning: a poplar tree with trembling leaves
second meaning: a fashionable skiing town in Colorado

explanation.surface: A film producer departs to stay at an American ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves producer' reads as a producer departing, but leaves are foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar tree known for its quivering foliage, and also a Colorado resort town.

clue.text: Not being served some egg or cream

blocks.note: a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu
the white is one part of an egg

explanation.surface: A diner is told that neither the egg dish nor the cream is available.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream as a colour is a pale yellowish shade that falls just short of pure white.

clue.text: Finally dance, as a finishing touch

blocks.note: for good means permanently, once and for all
a measure is an old word for a stately dance

explanation.surface: At the end of the evening there is a dance to round things off.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in addition to what is required, an extra flourish added beyond what is strictly necessary.

clue.text: Daughter needs to change in manner when woeful child appears-

indicators.note: changing the letters means rearranging them into a new form
in means placed inside, so the rearranged letters go within the word for manner

blocks.note: a way of doing something is a manner
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter must change her behaviour when a miserable child turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Monday's Child' says 'Wednesday's child is full of woe'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional rhyme the child born on this weekday is full of woe, so this is the day.

clue.text: Sue has one extra place inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the abbreviation for place goes into the word for extra

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
more means additional
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A woman named Sue has a spare room in her house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb meaning to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue in the old sense is to plead or petition earnestly, which is to beg desperately.

clue.text: Taken in, defeated - executed

indicators.note: an execution by beheading takes the head off, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: beaten means defeated

explanation.surface: Someone was tricked, beaten and then put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being fooled; here it means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed has been swallowed and ingested by the body.

clue.text: Work both ways to locate issue for one's counterpart

indicators.note: reading both ways means forwards then backwards, so the abbreviation is followed by its mirror

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work, and it is written forwards then backwards
to site something is to locate it
an issue of a magazine is a number

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to find a document for an associate.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names the person holding the equivalent role in another organisation or team.

clue.text: One polishes off something to read on beach

indicators.note: one thing sitting on another places it next to it, so the reading matter is joined to the beach

blocks.note: a beach is made of sand
a newspaper is something to read

explanation.surface: Someone finishes reading the newspaper while lying on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polishes off' suggests finishing a read quickly; here it is literal smoothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive paper rubs rough surfaces smooth, literally removing material when sanding wood.

clue.text: Ruler absolutely banning son in military HQ

indicators.note: to ban something is to keep it out, so that letter is removed from the ruler

blocks.note: a despot rules with absolute power
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An autocrat forbids his own son from entering army headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a regimental headquarters or base where troops are stationed and supplies kept.

clue.text: Pronounced downfall of regime

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word for a downfall is taken by its sound

blocks.note: rain is a downfall from the sky

explanation.surface: A marked collapse of a government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like 'marked' qualifying downfall, but it is the sound signal; downfall is weather, not collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the period of rule of a monarch or government, much as a regime is.

clue.text: Independently ring three times with different directions

indicators.note: the ring shape is used thrice, each time followed by its own set of compass points

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
north
a ring is round like the letter O
north, east and south
a ring is round like the letter O
west and north

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a number thrice, each time being given different instructions on how to get there.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on one's own means acting alone, without help or control from others.

clue.text: Liberal planning Norfolk holiday?

blocks.note: first meaning: tolerant and open to other views
second, playful meaning: having the Norfolk Broads in mind

explanation.surface: A member of the Liberal party is thinking about a holiday in Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England, popular for boating holidays; someone with them in mind is Broad-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal person is tolerant of other views and behaviour, which is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Wife and child I left only roof as shelter

indicators.note: left as in departed, so the letter I goes out of the word for child

blocks.note: my old Dutch is Cockney slang for one's wife
bairn is the Scottish word for a child

explanation.surface: A wife and child, abandoned, have nothing but a roof over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like abandoned; it is the departure of a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch barn is a farm structure with a curved roof on posts and no walls, sheltering hay.

clue.text: Archbishop of Canterbury once half lost in the wood

indicators.note: losing half means the first three of the six letters of the saint's name are dropped

blocks.note: St Anselm was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1093 to 1109

explanation.surface: A former archbishop got half lost wandering in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood timber taken from the tree of that name, so it names a kind of wood.

clue.text: Statesmen arranged financial review

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians set up an inquiry into the nation's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test is an official investigation into a person's income to assess eligibility for benefits.

clue.text: Fairy 16 finally has sex change

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the entry referred to by number
a change of sex swaps male for female, so one gender letter is swapped for the other

blocks.note: the answer to 16 across
the last letter of the answer to 16 across, standing for male

explanation.surface: A fairy undergoes a gender transition.
explanation.walkthrough: M and F are the usual abbreviations for male and female, so a sex change swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small mischievous supernatural being of folklore, a kind of fairy.

clue.text: Enemy, father said, may give us the slip

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a foe is an enemy and pa is father

explanation.surface: An enemy, says Dad, might slip away from us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give us the slip' suggests escaping, but a slip is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A social blunder is a slip, an embarrassing error of etiquette that someone might commit.

clue.text: Heavy re-edit ordered? Come off it!

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor is told to rework a text heavily and protests in disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Both exclamations express indignant disbelief at a suggestion, rejecting it as absurd or outrageous.

clue.text: It could give girl lift, on getting engaged at last

definitions.text: It could give girl lift, on getting engaged at last

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something turns it upwards, so the girl is read from bottom to top
at last points to the final letter of the word engaged

blocks.note: a maid is a girl
taken as written
the final letter of engaged

explanation.surface: Something that might cheer a young woman when she gets engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes an engagement ring stone lifting a fiancée's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is the traditional stone of an engagement ring, which delights the woman receiving it.

clue.text: Cause amazement about money needed up front for pastries

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word for causing amazement is read backwards
up front means placed at the beginning, so the money comes first

blocks.note: dough is slang for money
to stun is to cause amazement

explanation.surface: Something astonishing needs cash in advance, perhaps to pay for cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughnuts are rings or balls of sweet fried dough, a kind of pastry sold in bakeries.

clue.text: Appropriate fabric provided by mate of this seaman?

blocks.clueFragment: Appropriate fabric provided by mate of this seaman?
blocks.note: surface reading: a sailor's partner supplies suitable cloth
setter's reading: the Elizabethan sailor shares his name with a male bird whose mate, a duck, is also the name of a heavy cotton cloth

explanation.surface: A sailor's partner supplies the right cloth for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is a strong canvas-like fabric, and also the female mate of the male bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis was the famous Elizabethan navigator, and the word also names a male duck.

clue.text: Almost decided to conceal a muddle

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of decided is dropped
concealing something means hiding it inside, so the article goes within

blocks.note: to decide is to choose
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone nearly decided to hide a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is complete disorder and confusion, a muddle on a grand scale.

clue.text: Short spell in which I relax here?

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter of the word for spell is dropped
in which means something goes inside, so the I is placed within

blocks.note: a charm is a magic spell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brief period during which someone takes it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' reads as a stretch of time; it is magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a seat for one person, the place where somebody sits back and rests.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about old record's high class

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation is wrapped round the record

blocks.note: aha is an exclamation of surprise or discovery
an LP, or long-player, is an old vinyl record

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in surprise at an old vinyl album's superb quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the top grade in marking schemes, so it means first-class or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Unaccompanied, about to sing piece from Gondoliers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for unaccompanied goes round the verb

blocks.note: bare means alone, with nothing added
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: A soloist is set to perform a number from the Gilbert and Sullivan opera without accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like a hidden-word signal; it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian boat song traditionally sung by gondoliers as they row.

clue.text: Tragic scene of evil, in English tradition

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the wrongdoing sits within the English tradition

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
lore is a body of traditional knowledge
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: Evil acts staged in the English theatrical tradition make for a tragic setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore, the Danish castle at Helsingør, is where Shakespeare sets the tragedy Hamlet.

clue.text: Believe it may need extending, if one's short

definitions.text: it may need extending, if one's short

blocks.note: first meaning: to accept as true

blocks.clueFragment: it may need extending, if one's short
blocks.note: second meaning: a lender lets someone short of cash borrow more by extending this

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' suggests height, but it means short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to accept it as true; as a noun it is borrowing allowed by a lender.
